w07.126.q: This alternate zoning of the master universe, in association with the alternate clockwise and counterclockwise flow of the galaxies, is a factor in the stabilization of physical gravity designed to prevent the accentuation of gravity pressure to the point of disruptive and dispersive activities.

w07.127: Sadler links this balancing effect to the work of the Universal Absolute, the source of compensating motions that equalize the tensions set up by other motions. The boundaries of space can be summarized in four directions. The inner margin lies near Paradise but does not touch the Isle directly. Above and below, the midspace zones close it off. Between one level and the next lie quiet zones free of star dust; the one separating the superuniverses from the primary level averages about four hundred thousand light-years in width [12:1.14]. The outer margin extends beyond the master universe, though no one knows how far.
w07.129: Sadler finds what unites the six levels in the presence of the emerging God the Ultimate.

w07.130.q: The Ultimate is, or sometime will be, space present to the outer margins of the fourth space level.

w07.131: As a Creative Spirit's space presence marks out the extent of a local universe, the Ultimate's space presence marks out the extent of the master universe. The oversight of the Master Architects, likewise, begins at Paradise and ends at the outer edge of the outermost level. Let us now set out from peripheral Paradise, pass through midspace and the inner margin of actual space, and walk outward.
w07.132: Havona has twelve circuits in all: three of satellites, seven of the billion worlds, and two belts of dark gravity bodies. The inner ten circuits revolve clockwise; of the dark gravity bodies, the inner belt moves counterclockwise and the outer belt clockwise. The dark gravity bodies are a unique kind of matter, neither triata nor gravita, and because of their mass the central universe outweighs all seven superuniverses together [12:1.10].
w07.133: The seven superuniverses revolve counterclockwise and share the superuniverse space level among them. Our own Orvonton corresponds roughly to the astronomers' Milky Way and is divided into ten major sectors, each with one hundred minor sectors. The center of our minor sector lies in the Sagittarius star cloud. The text reports that the outermost inhabited system is a little less than a quarter of a million light-years from the center of the superuniverse [32:2.11], and on that basis Sadler puts Orvonton's diameter at roughly half a million light-years.
w07.134: The outer space levels are not yet organized or inhabited. The finaliters are believed to be destined for service there, and the organization of those regions will mark the beginning of a transcendental and subabsolute approach to God [0:8.12]. The text says that new telescopes will reveal some 375 million galaxies in outer space [12:2.3], and it also says this:

w07.135.q: It is increasingly the belief of all Uversa that the assembling Corps of the Finality are destined to some future service in the universes of outer space, where we already are able to identify the clustering of at least seventy thousand aggregations of matter, each of which is greater than any one of the present superuniverses.

w07.136: Sadler takes both statements to describe the same matter: the 375 million galaxies being organized into seventy thousand aggregations on the Primary Space Level. The more distant levels, he believes, are hidden from our telescopes by cosmic dust.

w07.137.q: But about one-half million light-years beyond the periphery of the present grand universe we observe the beginnings of a zone of an unbelievable energy action which increases in volume and intensity for over twenty-five million light-years.

w07.138: Sadler's reckoning runs like this. If the energy action grows stronger for over twenty-five million light-years, it presumably weakens again over a similar span, so the primary level would be about fifty million light-years wide, a hundred times the breadth of the superuniverse level. If each of the seventy thousand aggregations is larger than a superuniverse, then the primary level already outweighs all seven superuniverses by a factor of more than ten thousand (70,000 ÷ 7). On the secondary level, early evidence of force has been detected more than fifty million light-years beyond the phenomena of the primary level [12:1.15]. On the tertiary level a tendency toward clockwise rotation has begun to be sensed, while of the quartan level nothing is known except that it exists. Sadler judges the quartan level to be physically still wholly dormant.

w07.149: The sevenfold increase in the number of Architects from one outer level to the next is one more clue to the relative scale of the levels. Standing at the outer edge of the quartan level and "looking" outward, one would see endless empty space: the region beyond the master universe. Sadler believes the Master Architects understand how the master universe is related to something greater that lies beyond it.

w07.150.q: Even space itself is but an ultimate condition, a condition of qualification within the relative absoluteness of the quiet zones of midspace.

w07.151: Sadler and the text: a few numbers and references
w07.152: Sadler cites the space presence of the Ultimate as 12:6.3, but the statement actually appears at 12:6.13; likewise, the fifty million light-years of the secondary level are found at 12:1.15, not 12:1.14. The original gives the number of Architects for the tertiary level as 3,420, whereas the text says 3,430 [31:9.8], and only the latter figure makes the seven groups total 28,011. The distance Sadler uses as Orvonton's radius is, strictly speaking, the distance from the outermost inhabited systems to the center. The width and mass of the primary level are Sadler's estimates derived from the text.
w07.153: 4. Postscript: The Paradox of World Pictures (orig. pp. 187–189)
w07.154: Sadler observes that The Urantia Book rigorously refrains from mentioning the theory of relativity and depicts the geography of the master universe in Newtonian terms. He conjectures two reasons. One is intelligibility: a text written for ordinary readers must convey its meaning in words rather than in mathematical symbols. The other concerns the size of the error: Newton's concepts may involve "less distortion" than Einstein's. Sadler's personal belief is that both reasons were at work.
w07.155: Four world pictures as Sadler arranges them
w07.157: Natural to the senses, but the retrograde motion of the planets had to be forcibly explained away
w07.158: Circular orbits did not fit until elliptical orbits made everything simpler
w07.159: Unavoidable, since science cannot infer an unmoving Isle; relativity theory belongs here
w07.160: Having a center, it allows for absolute motion
w07.161: Sadler remarks that every world picture has had its own "phlogiston," a rationalization devised to cover facts that did not fit. Relativity theory, he suspects, shows traces of the same thing and may break down in the remote regions of the master universe; he cites an astronomer's objection from the time of his writing, together with the text's statement that space may eventually neutralize linear gravity. This is best read as Sadler's personal view of a scientific debate of his own day.
w07.162: The world picture of The Urantia Book has a center. The alternating procession of the space levels is absolute motion, measured against the unmoving Isle of Paradise.

w07.163.q: 3. Relative motions—relative in the sense that they are not evaluated with Paradise as a base point. Primary and secondary motions are absolute, motion in relation to unmoving Paradise.

w07.164: In the largest sense, perhaps, Newton's centered universe distorts the facts less than Einstein's centerless one. That is the question Sadler leaves with his readers.
w07.165: Space is either unpervaded or pervaded, and the master universe is built within the pervaded space that extends horizontally from Paradise.
w07.166: The Urantia Book treats space as a positive reality that contains and conditions motion; the limit of space is where midspace begins.
w07.167: The six space levels are elliptical regions of motion separated by quiet zones, and their alternating directions of rotation stabilize gravity pressure.
w07.168: The master universe extends as far as the Ultimate is space present: to the outer margin of the fourth space level.
w07.169: The farther out a level lies, the less is known about it, while the number of assigned Master Architects increases sevenfold; the width and mass of the primary level are Sadler's estimates.
w07.170: Sadler attributes the revelation's avoidance of relativity theory to intelligibility and "less distortion," and presents the Paradise-centered world picture as a universe in which absolute motion is possible.
